narrative:
The model estimated a 25.0% probability of bad credit—about a one-in-four chance that repayment would become problematic. That estimate was high enough under this lender’s approval cutoff to decline the application; it is a risk estimate, not a certainty.

The ranking shows what most influenced your result. The strongest factor was the requested term: nine months, well below the approved average of about 19 months, and this worked in your favor by lowering assessed risk. The second was the business purpose of the loan; although business use is uncommon among approved applicants (8.7%), it also pushed your score toward good credit. The third was your checking-account balance of 0–200 DM, which increased risk; approved applicants more often show no checking account, and only 18.4% have this balance range. So the two most influential factors helped you, but the checking-account signal and the rest of your profile still left the combined assessment above the lender’s decline threshold.

Next, ask the lender for the specific reasons and whether a manual review or appeal is available. Check that your account and application details are accurate. To strengthen a future application, focus on steady account balances, avoiding overdrafts, building savings, and providing evidence that the business loan is viable. Reapply only when you can show a stronger repayment profile.
